papers_read.title_as_printed: MC-ViViT: Multi-branch Classifier-ViViT to detect Mild Cognitive Impairment in older adults using facial videos (Sun, Dodge & Mahoor, Expert Systems With Applications 238 (2024) 121929)
Mild cognitive impairment detection from facial video interviews by applying spatial-to-temporal attention module (Alsuhaibani, Dodge & Mahoor, Expert Systems With Applications 252 (2024) 124185)

what_each_reports.P-76: I-CONECT facial videos, four themes (Crafts Hobbies 32 videos, Day Time TV Shows 41, Movie Genres 35, School Subjects 39), subject-disjoint K-fold (3 videos per fold): accuracy 90.63% (29/32) / 85.37% / 85.71% / 89.74%, AUC 0.60 / 0.50 / 0.61 / 0.53 (Table 2); cross-theme 80.5-85.7%.
what_each_reports.P-77: I-CONECT facial videos from the intervention arm, four different themes (Summertime 30 videos, Self-Care 30, Halloween 32, Cities and Towns 39), 10-fold subject CV: accuracy 83.3% / 66.7% / 87.5% (28/32) / 79.5%, AUC 0.83 / 0.66 / 0.87 / 0.80 (Table 4); five reshuffles give means 74.6 / 61.3 / 84.4 / 78.0%. Table 5 lists P-76 (Sun et al. 2024) at 90.6% accuracy, AUC 0.6, and the text concedes 'other models have achieved better accuracy and F1 score'.

quantity_a: Video-level accuracy/AUC of MC-ViViT for MCI vs NC on four I-CONECT conversation themes (32-41 videos each), subject-disjoint K-fold.
quantity_b: Video-level accuracy/AUC of CAE+STAM for MCI vs NC on four other I-CONECT themes (30-39 quality-screened videos each), 10-fold CV.
incompatible_if_same: No. Best-theme accuracies are 29/32 (90.63%) vs 28/32 (87.5%), a one-video difference on about 32 videos, well within sampling noise; both papers conclude facial video discriminates MCI. P-77 explicitly accepts P-76's higher accuracy and claims only a higher AUC, which P-76's own table (AUC 0.50-0.61) does not dispute.

gates.dataset_family: match: I-CONECT, but different conversation themes and different (overlapping) participant subsets per theme.
gates.validation_tier: match: both internal subject-disjoint cross-validation, no external cohort.

endpoint_and_metric: compatible metric types (accuracy, AUC), but the video sets differ by theme and by quality screening, so the per-theme accuracies are estimates on different samples.
performance_validity: not a performance disagreement; neither value reaches 0.97.
independence: Not independent: same senior authors (H. H. Dodge, M. H. Mahoor), same laboratory, same trial (I-CONECT) with overlapping participants.
grounds: The two results agree in direction: both papers conclude that facial video discriminates MCI from normal cognition.
The accuracy gap (29/32 vs 28/32 on about 32 videos per theme) is within sampling noise, and the videos come from different themes.
P-77 itself cites P-76's 90.6% accuracy and concedes it, claiming superiority only in AUC; neither paper refutes a claim of the other.
The papers share senior authors and the trial dataset, so they are not independent in any case.

evidence_quotes.quote: Our experimental results on the I-CONECT dataset show the great potential of MC-ViViT in predicting MCI with a high accuracy of 90.63% accuracy on some of the interview videos.
MC-ViViT predicts 29 out of 32 subjects correctly on the theme Crafts Hobbies, which reaches the highest accuracy, 90.63%.
The average AUC of all four themes is 0.56.

The detection accuracy using this combined method reached 88%, whereas the accuracy without applying the segments and sequences information of the facial features within a video on a certain theme was 84%.
Sun et al. (2024) Visual 90.6% 0.93 0.6 Ours Visual 87.5% 0.89 0.87
Although other models have achieved better accuracy and F1 score, our proposed framework achieved the highest AUC on the I-CONECT dataset.

record_defects: dataset_family_equivalence true without noting the shared authorship and the use of different conversation themes; the record does not record the non-independence.
registry Sample_N_Approx for P-77 is 68 (intervention-arm participants); the analysed samples are 30-39 quality-screened videos per theme.
resolution_status 'partially_resolved_candidate' is not supported: the bridging-evidence list is unrelated headline scores, and there is no disagreement to resolve.
what_would_change_the_verdict: Only if the two models were run on the same theme and videos and one paper's result excluded the other's; no such evaluation exists in either paper.
